subject: Aperture Systems — Dedicated Capacity RFP: reservation commitment checklist
messages:
From: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@aperture.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Dedicated Capacity — GPU mix, throughput targets, and reservation planning

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this RFP. We're running a procurement for a year-long dedicated inference reservation to support Aperture's flagship agent product. Attached is the RFP package (aperture_rfp_package.pdf) and a short checklist we ask vendors to complete. High-level ask: provide a plan for GPU family mix, per-model throughput targets, tail-latency expectations, and a phased reservation that allows scaling from pilot -> production with clear breakpoints.

Specific items we care about:
- Minimum and recommended GPU SKUs for 7B/13B/70B families
- Expected tokens/sec and p99 tail latency for each SKU at target QPS and for 2x burst windows
- Slotting approach when demand is bursty (how do you prevent noisy neighbors?)
- Quantization and fallback model recommendations to reduce cost while preserving quality
- Billing/commitment terms and any ramp flexibility (monthly vs quarterly true-up)

Can you complete the attached workbook and return by EOD Friday 18 Sep PST? We'd like to schedule a 45-minute technical alignment on Monday 21 Sep.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Miles
Head of Platform Procurement
Aperture Systems

Attachment: aperture_rfp_package.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@aperture.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Capacity — GPU mix, throughput targets, and reservation planning

Sarah — thanks for the RFP and the checklist. We're on it. We've filled the initial workbook with a baseline (pilot -> steady state -> peak) and included three commitment scenarios tied to throughput and GPU mix. Attached: aperture_rfi_workbook_v1.xlsx and redwood-dedicated-term-sheet.pdf (term sheet is intentionally high-level; we can iterate).

Quick summary of our recommended approach (full detail in workbook):
- Pilot (30 days): small pool using mixed A10g-equivalent V1 nodes for validation of tokenization, caching effectiveness, and prefix reuse; expected p95 generation latency under 150ms for 7B models with batching=auto.
- Production baseline (steady state): blend of quantized A40-equivalent for cost-sensitive 13B workloads and a small set of H100-equivalent for 70B low-latency routes. Target throughput: ~120M tokens/day baseline with 2x burst for promotions.
- Peak/fallback: automated routing to quantized variants plus burst lanes using pre-warmed slots; when capacity constrained, fallback to a 13B quantized variant with 2–4% quality delta on most prompts.

Open items we need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Distribution of request types (chat vs single-shot generation vs embeddings) and average prompt+response token counts per route
2) Acceptable tail-latency SLOs (p95 vs p99) per route
3) Whether you require dedicated isolation for PII-sensitive routes (this affects packing/slotting rules)

Can you confirm whether the workbook deadline is firm? If EOD Friday is tight, we can deliver a prioritized workbook (pilot + baseline) by Friday and the full commitment scenarios by Monday.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: aperture_rfi_workbook_v1.xlsx (Excel workbook), redwood-dedicated-term-sheet.pdf (PDF)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Capacity — quick technical clarifications

Jonas — adding a few technical notes we should include in the workbook answers: 
- GPU family guidance: for 7B models, 2-way A10g-equivalent packing with continuous batching is usually ideal. For 13B quantized int4, A40-equivalent provides best cost/latency. For 70B production routes, H100-equivalent with NVLink-enabled multi-GPU shards gives reliable p99 under tight budgets.
- Throughput numbers (rough): on A40-equivalent single card expect ~300–600 tokens/sec for 13B quantized (batching dependent); H100-equivalent single card for 70B ~150–300 tokens/sec. Call these starting points — we'll surface exact runbook numbers in the workbook's appendix.
- Tail-latency mitigation: recommend KV cache pre-warming for frequent sessions and a short-lived request-level cache for common prefixes (saves ~15–30% tokens served).

I'll add the appendix table with microbenchmarks before we send.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@aperture.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@aperture.ai>, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Capacity — follow-up questions on slotting and bursts

Jonas — thanks for the workbook draft. Couple clarifying questions pulled from the team after a quick review: 
1) You mention a 2x burst window for promotions — can you show an example slotting plan that demonstrates how you would absorb a 48-hour sustained 2x load without violating other customers' SLAs? Please include pre-warm, burst-lane sizing, and fallback sequencing.
2) For routes that process PII, we need assurance about packing (no multi-tenant packing for PII routes). Can you enumerate which of your proposed SKUs would be dedicated-only vs packable?
3) Pricing: is the term sheet's ramp mechanism monthly true-up or quarterly true-up? Aperture prefers monthly true-up for financial forecasting.

Quote for context:
> On Wed, Sep 16, 2026 at 10:07 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 
> > Quick summary of our recommended approach (full detail in workbook):
> > - Pilot (30 days): small pool using mixed A10g-equivalent V1 nodes for validation...
> > - Production baseline (steady state): blend of quantized A40-equivalent for 13B workloads and a small set of H100-equivalent for 70B low-latency routes.

We'd like a short deliverable (1-page slotting diagram + table) that shows: typical baseline pool size, additional pre-warm nodes for a 48-hour 2x event, and the sequence (pre-warm -> burst-lane -> fallback) with explicit counts. Can you return by Monday morning PST?

Thanks,
Marco
Senior Product Ops, Aperture Systems

Attachment referenced: aperture_rfp_team_notes.txt (text, 4KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@aperture.ai>, Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@aperture.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Capacity — slotting diagram, commitment scenarios, and next steps

Marco / Sarah — attached is the 1-page slotting diagram and three commitment scenarios that align to your ask. Key points summarized below (full numbers in commitment_scenarios.pdf / appendix in the workbook):

- Baseline pool: 20 A40-equivalent cards for 13B quantized routes + 4 H100-equivalent cards reserved for 70B latency-sensitive traffic. Baseline supports ~120M tokens/day with headroom for typical growth.
- 48-hour 2x event handling: pre-warm strategy uses 25% warm standby (5 A40-equivalent cards) plus a burst-lane of 8 additional A40-equivalent instances spun up on reserved burst capacity. If utilization still exceeds thresholds, we automatically route non-PII routes to quantized fallbacks and shed low-priority background jobs. This sequence keeps external neighbor SLAs intact because burst-lane uses dedicated reserved capacity and pre-warm is allocated from your committed pool.
- PII packing: we mark routes as dedicated-only; those will never be packed with other tenants. Per your requirement, dedicated-only routes are pinned to isolated H100 or dedicated A40 equivalents depending on model size.
- True-up: we support monthly true-up with a quarterly reconciliation window as an optional concession; see term sheet.

Next steps:
1) Shared Drive: slotting diagram and workbook appendix (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ApertureRFP).
2) Commitment scenarios PDF attached (commitment_scenarios.pdf).
3) If this aligns, we'll send a DocuSign link for the starter commitment (pilot -> baseline) — link provided: https://www.docusign.net/commit/APTR-2026-0919.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on review. Happy to run the Monday alignment call at 10am PST — please confirm.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: commitment_scenarios.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
